events.ai_basis: OpenAI language-model systems were used extensively in the discovery, computational search, verification, and preparation of this work.

events.credibility_reason: Single X post that was never read; no non-colourability check of the 68-vertex graph appears in any source, and its date rests on MathWorld alone.

why: The statement makes one universal claim, so a single explicit bridgeless cubic graph with no Petersen colouring answers all of it (scope whole, counterexample, refuted), given the cubic equivalence between P-colourings and cycle-continuous maps that the sources state. Putman's 112-vertex graph counts as digested: Jooken, a named combinatorialist who did not write Putman's paper, published a separate hand proof that this same graph is non-colourable, and that is a verification by a third party. Jooken's own preprint, the 52-vertex Zenodo record and the arXiv v3 have no outside reader yet, so they are unreviewed. Putman's AI role was the close call. The authors' own sentence lists 'discovery' and 'computational search' among what the OpenAI systems were used for, which goes beyond checking or writing and means the systems contributed to finding the graph. But it does not say the model produced the graph, and a human author designed and took responsibility for the work, so I answered assisted rather than generated. Jooken's ChatGPT use (proofreading, rewriting, figures) is not in ai.systems and is write-up work, so I answered none. The 68-vertex announcement's credit to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra is second-hand and its ai.systems is empty, so I answered none and doubtful. Every event before the snapshot either checks finitely many graphs, settles a changed question, reformulates the problem, or covers a restricted family (Sedlar–Škrekovski, case).
doubts: Putman's assisted (not generated) rests on a vague provenance sentence; an account from the author of who found the graph could raise it to generated. Digestion of Putman's graph relies on Jooken's hand proof, whose body the researcher did not read; Jooken is also a co-author of the competing 52-vertex work. The 68-vertex X post may be credited to GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, but that credit could not be confirmed at source. The cycle-continuous equivalence was not checked at source.
